Take web development for example. The W3C set the standards for HTML, Javascript, CSS, etc... and for the longest time, browser manufacturers only implemented what they wanted from the standards and left the rest unimplemented. Adding to that problem, all the browser manufacturers all had different things they wanted to implement - meaning that all the browsers didn't even support the same technologies as one another. This led to an ecosystem where devs had to make as many versions of a webpage as there were browsers - and then extras for older/newer versions - and all the while, better ideas people had for building their webapps were impossible because they required technology that was in the standards that NO browser had implemented yet.

Webdev was an absolute fucking nightmare for over a decade, until devs started pressuring browser manufacturers to implement the entire standard. At first, they were met with resistance, but then they came up with the brilliant idea of creating and publicizing tests for browsers (called ACID) and basically using the results from these tests to advertise and push for users to use the best browser of the bunch. This kicked the browser manufacturers in the ass and forced them to truly compete against each other by being the first to fully implement the standard.

Now webdev is much simpler, and we all have fewer ulcers and stress heart attacks - and the internet is far more technologically advanced because of it.
